sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, standing in a poised neutral pose, showing the card-panel front. Panel 2: full-body true side profile, showing how flat the card panel is over the crinoline. Panel 3: full-body back view showing the card-back pattern of the panel. Panel 4 (tall right column): head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera, neutral expression, face clearly lit. Each full-body figure is drawn a little small inside its panel, complete from the top of the head to the hem of the gown and the floor with clear space above and below, standing on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow; if any part is cut off by the panel edge the sheet is wrong. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels.

Subject: ONE courtier of the royal procession, alone on the sheet: a lady about 35 years old, a real human actress. Slender and elegant, about 166 cm tall. Dark brown hair in smooth centre-parted bands and a low chignon; brown eyes; poised, slightly supercilious expression. Her dress follows the group rule, quoted verbatim from the costume bible: 'an 1862 royal procession in card costume: ten elegant courtiers, ladies and gentlemen, in scarlet-and-gold court dress, crinoline gowns and tail coats, covered by flat ivory playing-card panels with bright red diamond pips and stitched all over with small red diamond-shaped paste ornaments; and ten small children in ivory card tunics and pinafores with crimson heart pips over crimson-and-white children's dress, girls in short full skirts with white pantalettes, boys in tunic suits, with many little crimson heart appliques; the backs of all panels in a crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette; festive and immaculate'. On this one courtier that means: a scarlet-and-gold 1862 crinoline court gown with a modest neckline, covered front and back by a flat ivory playing-card panel; the front panel is the Three of Diamonds, with exactly three bright red diamond pips in a vertical line and a small '3' index with a small diamond in the top-left and bottom-right corners; small red diamond-shaped paste ornaments stitched all over her sleeves and skirt. No heart symbol on the front.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.

Layout recap (highest priority): four separate panels side by side, exactly one lady in each panel, the same woman in front / side / back full-body views and one head-and-shoulders close-up; no children, no other figures.
